authority.legal_name: Brisbane City Council ferry services (CityCat / CityHopper / Cross River), operated under Translink
authority.geography_type: a winding tidal river through the heart of the city

mandate.summary: Brisbane City Council runs the CityCat, CityHopper and Cross River ferry network on the Brisbane River — about 25 terminals forming the spine of inner-city public transport, ticketed through Translink and carrying roughly 5 million trips a year. It is one of the most successful urban river-ferry systems in the world.
current_priorities: Run the ~25-terminal CityCat / CityHopper / Cross River network on the Brisbane River
Deliver the all-electric CityCat commitment — new battery-electric CityCats replacing diesel vessels
Be transport-ready for the Brisbane 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games
Extend terminals upriver and downriver as the city and its riverfront precincts grow

policy_targets.vision: Brisbane City Council carbon-neutral commitment; all-electric CityCat fleet program; Brisbane 2032 transport plan
policy_targets.decarb_note: Brisbane City Council has committed to an all-electric CityCat fleet, replacing diesel vessels with new battery-electric CityCats as part of the city's carbon-neutral goals.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the CityCat network — fast, low-wake hops along the river spine (UQ St Lucia through the city to Northshore Hamilton) and quiet cross-river links that complement the all-electric CityCat program without disturbing the wake-sensitive residential reaches.

precedent.headline: Brisbane's CityCat network carries roughly 5 million trips a year across ~25 river terminals — a globally admired urban ferry system, now going all-electric.
precedent.network: CityCat express, CityHopper free inner-city, and Cross River services link UQ St Lucia, West End, South Bank, the CBD (North Quay / QUT Gardens Point / Riverside), New Farm, Teneriffe, Bulimba, Hawthorne and Northshore Hamilton along the Brisbane River.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the CityCat network — fast, low-wake hops along the river spine (UQ St Lucia through the city to Northshore Hamilton) and quiet cross-river links that complement the all-electric CityCat program without disturbing the wake-sensitive residential reaches.

domestic_pairs.rationale: The flagship campus-to-city run — UQ St Lucia up through West End to North Quay in the CBD.
South Bank to Riverside — the busiest cultural-to-CBD cross-reach in the city centre.
The full river spine — North Quay through New Farm and Bulimba down to Northshore Hamilton.
Riverside to Bulimba — a heavy commute leg into the eastern suburbs.
Holman Street, Kangaroo Point, to Riverside — the CityHopper inner-city cross-river hop.
Teneriffe to Bulimba — the cross-river link between two riverside village precincts.
New Farm Park to QUT Gardens Point — a riverside-park-to-university commute leg.
Hawthorne to North Quay — an eastern-suburb express commute into the city.

regional_links.note: The CityCat network is entirely domestic on the Brisbane River. There are no international or open-sea legs — the whole proposal is domestic, inside sheltered river water.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.hazard: Tight river meanders & strong tidal flow
hazards.detail: The Brisbane River winds in tight bends with a strong tidal stream; hand-waypoint the channel through every meander and account for the set on the bends.
After major floods (2011, 2022) the river carries logs and debris; routing must follow the maintained navigation channel and the council's post-flood advisories.
Victoria Bridge, the Go Between Bridge, William Jolly Bridge and the Story Bridge piers constrain the central reaches; route through the marked navigation spans with air-draft and pier clearance.
The upper (UQ / West End) and lower reaches have shoal edges and sandbars; hand-waypoint the dredged channel and account for tide height.
Long stretches of the river are lined with homes, pontoons and rowing clubs; strict low-wake operation and no-foil zones are required through the residential and rowing reaches.
CityCats, CityHoppers, recreational craft and University rowing crews share the narrow river; geofence speed and give-way behaviour at the busy CBD and UQ reaches.
